title: Full citizen registration through to a usable funded wallet
preconditions: A clean citizen applicant with all assets available
steps:
1. Complete every step end to end
2. Sign in
3. Fund the wallet and make one transaction
expected: Registration, sign-in, funding and the first transaction all succeed on the same identity; profile, wallet and ledger agree throughout

title: Nafath approval carries the verified identity into the application
preconditions: A citizen applicant reaching the Nafath step
steps:
1. Complete Nafath authentication and approve in the Nafath app
2. Return to registration
3. Compare the stored identity fields against what Nafath returned
expected: The application proceeds with the identity Nafath returned; no identity field is taken from user input where Nafath is authoritative

title: Nafath rejection stops the application without creating an account
preconditions: An applicant at the Nafath step
steps:
1. Reject the request in the Nafath app
2. Inspect the application and search for any created account or wallet
expected: The application is stopped with a clear reason; no account, profile or wallet is created

title: An expired Nafath or Yaqeen TTL blocks progress
preconditions: An application whose Nafath or Yaqeen data has passed its TTL
steps:
1. Attempt to continue the application
2. Attempt to sign in once the account exists
expected: Progress is blocked and re-verification is required; stale identity data is never accepted as current (EMI-5836)

title: Registration OTPs are delivered and never stored in plain text
preconditions: An applicant at any OTP step
steps:
1. Trigger each registration OTP
2. Inspect the notification log and the Taqnyat HTTP log
expected: Each OTP is delivered and every stored copy is hashed; no plain-text OTP is persisted anywhere (EMI-5913)

title: A completed registration provisions exactly one wallet
preconditions: An applicant completing registration end to end
steps:
1. Complete registration
2. Query the wallets created for the account
expected: Exactly one main wallet exists, with the correct currency and a zero opening balance across all four buckets

title: Wathiq CR data populates the business profile and is not user-editable
preconditions: A business applicant with a valid CRN
steps:
1. Enter the CRN and let Wathiq resolve it
2. Attempt to edit the returned legal name, CR status and activity fields
expected: Wathiq-sourced fields populate the profile and are read-only; a user cannot overwrite registry data

title: An inactive or expired CR is refused at registration
preconditions: A CRN that Wathiq reports as expired or inactive
steps: 1. Submit it
expected: Registration is refused with a clear reason; no account is created for a business that is not currently registered

title: Wathiq failure does not silently fall back to user-entered data
preconditions: Wathiq made unreachable
steps: 1. Submit a CRN and observe the outcome
expected: The step fails visibly and the application waits; the platform never proceeds on unverified user-entered company data

title: Yaqeen verification result gates the application
preconditions: An applicant subject to Yaqeen verification
steps:
1. Complete the flow for a passing and a failing result
2. Attempt to continue in each case
expected: A pass allows progress and a fail stops it with a neutral reason; the outcome is recorded against the application for audit

title: Yaqeen unavailable does not let an application through unverified
preconditions: Yaqeen made unreachable
steps: 1. Reach the verification step
expected: The application waits and is retried; it never proceeds as verified when verification did not run

title: The verified IBAN is the one carried into the wallet and first payout
preconditions: A completed registration with a verified IBAN
steps:
1. Complete registration
2. Compare the IBAN on the profile, the wallet and the first outbound instruction
expected: All three carry the same verified IBAN; nothing re-reads an unverified user-entered value later in the chain

title: Uploaded documents are stored, retrievable and scanned
preconditions: An applicant uploading the required documents
steps:
1. Upload each document type
2. Retrieve each and check storage controls
expected: Each is stored under the applicable encryption and access controls, retrievable intact, and rejected if it fails the configured type and size rules

title: Lean IBAN verification maps failures to the right error, without retrying a 4xx
preconditions: An applicant submitting an IBAN for verification
steps:
1. Submit a valid IBAN
2. Submit one Lean rejects with a 4xx
3. Force a 5xx and observe retries
expected: The valid IBAN verifies; the 4xx fails fast as LEAN_VERIFICATION_FAILED with no retry in the logs; the 5xx retries to the configured maximum then fails (EMI-5927)

title: Nafath timeout is recoverable without restarting registration
preconditions: An applicant at the Nafath step
steps:
1. Let the Nafath request expire unanswered
2. Retry from the same session
expected: The applicant is told the request expired and can retry; entered data is preserved and the session is not destroyed

title: Nafath unavailable is surfaced as a service error, not a rejection
preconditions: Nafath made unreachable
steps: 1. Reach the Nafath step
expected: A service-unavailable state is shown and the application is left resumable; the applicant is never told they were rejected because a third party was down

title: A refreshed registration session continues the same application
preconditions: An application held past its original session lifetime
steps:
1. Let the registration session refresh
2. Continue to the next step
expected: The same application continues with data intact; the registration refresh is isolated from the login refresh mechanism (EMI-5995)

title: Tahaqaq verification result gates the application consistently
preconditions: An applicant subject to Tahaqaq verification
steps: 1. Complete the flow for a passing and a failing result
expected: A pass allows progress and a fail stops it with a neutral reason; the outcome is recorded against the application for audit

title: Registration holds up under concurrent applications
preconditions: Load profile representative of a campaign peak
steps:
1. Drive concurrent registrations through the identity and verification steps
2. Measure step latency and error rate
expected: Latency stays within the agreed budget and no application is lost, duplicated or cross-contaminated between concurrent sessions

title: A slow third party degrades one step, not the whole flow
preconditions: Nafath or Wathiq responding slowly
steps:
1. Introduce latency at the third party
2. Observe the affected step and the rest of the application
expected: The affected step times out cleanly with a retry path; unrelated steps and other applicants are unaffected

title: Callback ingestion sustains terminal peak load
preconditions: Peak terminal callback volume
steps: 1. Drive sustained callback load and measure ingestion latency and error rate
expected: Every callback is ingested exactly once within the agreed latency; none is dropped under load

title: Every admin configuration change is audit-logged
preconditions: Audit log accessible
steps:
1. Make several configuration changes
2. Inspect the audit trail
expected: Each is recorded with actor, timestamp, previous and new values; no change is applied without a record

title: A commission configuration change reaches live pricing
preconditions: An active commission scheme
steps:
1. Change the rate
2. Complete a transaction of that type
3. Inspect the fee entries
expected: The new rate applies without a release and the fee entries match it exactly

title: A limit change applies to new transactions and not retrospectively
preconditions: A wallet with existing transactions and a limit about to change
steps:
1. Change the limit
2. Attempt transactions either side of the new value
3. Re-read historical transactions
expected: New transactions follow the new limit; historical ones are unchanged and are not re-evaluated

title: A fee matrix change prices the next transaction correctly
preconditions: An active fee matrix
steps:
1. Change a fee
2. Complete a transaction of that type
3. Inspect the fee entries
expected: The new fee applies without a release and the entries match it exactly; historical transactions are not re-priced

title: A partner bank configuration change routes payments correctly
preconditions: More than one partner bank configured
steps:
1. Change the routing configuration
2. Complete an outbound payment
expected: The payment routes to the configured bank and the instruction carries that bank's details

title: Card management settings reach card behaviour
preconditions: Configurable card settings
steps:
1. Change a setting
2. Exercise the affected card behaviour
expected: The change takes effect on the next transaction without a release

title: A wallet configuration change propagates to the wallet service
preconditions: A configurable wallet rule
steps: 1. Change it and exercise the affected behaviour
expected: The change takes effect on the wallet service without a restart, and the previous value stops applying

title: A scheduled job change from the admin panel takes effect
preconditions: A job registered in the Jobs section
steps:
1. Change its schedule, then disable it
2. Observe the next run windows
expected: The schedule change takes effect and the disabled job does not run; run history records both

title: Admin staff creation notifies without leaking internal detail
preconditions: Admin staff creation available
steps: 1. Create a staff user and inspect the notification
expected: The notification reaches the right recipient and carries no tenant number or other internal identifier (EMI-5838)

title: Admin list screens page within budget at production volume
preconditions: Production-scale admin data
steps: 1. Load and deep-page the main admin lists, measuring response time
expected: Each stays within the agreed budget with indexed access and no full-table scan

title: Commission and VAT post to their own wallets exactly once
preconditions: Transactions of each type that carries commission
steps:
1. Complete each
2. Inspect the commission and VAT wallet ledgers
expected: Each transaction produces exactly one commission and one VAT entry; the sum of every leg equals what left the payer to the halalah

title: Every transaction type posts to the ledger consistently
preconditions: One completed transaction of each supported type
steps: 1. For each, compare the transaction record, its ledger postings and the running balance
expected: All three agree for every type; the four-bucket identity holds on every participating wallet after each posting

title: A pending transaction resolves without stranding a reserve
preconditions: Transactions that will settle and fail from pending
steps:
1. Drive one to settlement and one to failure
2. Inspect all four buckets on every participating wallet
expected: Each resolves cleanly with no reserve left behind on any leg, including commission and VAT

title: Externally-settled transactions match the bank statement
preconditions: A trading day with external movements and its statement
steps: 1. Reconcile the day's transactions against the statement
expected: Every externally-settled transaction matches a statement line; anything unmatched surfaces as an exception rather than passing silently

title: Transaction throughput holds at peak without lost postings
preconditions: Peak concurrent transaction load
steps:
1. Drive sustained mixed transaction load
2. Reconcile the ledger against what was submitted
expected: Every submitted transaction is accounted for exactly once; none is lost, duplicated or left in an intermediate state

title: Every balance-changing transaction notifies the right parties
preconditions: Notifications enabled
steps:
1. Complete transactions of several types
2. Inspect notifications for each party
expected: Each party is notified with the correct amount and counterparty; nothing sensitive is stored in plain text

title: The transaction log query stays indexed at production volume
preconditions: A production-scale transaction log
steps: 1. Query and deep-page the log with filters, capturing query plans
expected: Indexed access only, no full-table scan, and response time stays within the agreed budget

title: Sign in, transact and sign out on one continuous session
preconditions: An active account with a funded wallet
steps:
1. Sign in with OTP
2. Complete a transaction
3. Sign out
4. Attempt to reuse the previous session token
expected: The whole flow completes on one session; after sign-out the token is rejected and no authenticated call succeeds with it

title: Nafath-based sign-in resolves to the right account
preconditions: An account enrolled for Nafath sign-in
steps:
1. Sign in through Nafath and approve
2. Inspect the session's account and privileges
expected: The session belongs to the account Nafath authenticated, with that account's privileges and no other

title: Sign-in is blocked when Nafath or Yaqeen data has expired
preconditions: An account whose identity data has passed its TTL
steps: 1. Attempt to sign in
expected: Sign-in is blocked with a clear re-verification path; stale identity data never grants a session (EMI-5836)

title: Sign-in OTPs are delivered and stored hashed
preconditions: An account requiring OTP at sign-in
steps: 1. Sign in and inspect the notification and HTTP logs
expected: The OTP is delivered and every stored copy is hashed; no plain-text value is persisted

title: A business whose CR has lapsed cannot transact after sign-in
preconditions: A business whose CR expires after onboarding
steps:
1. Sign in
2. Attempt a transaction
expected: Either sign-in or the transaction is blocked per the documented rule, and the reason is explicit rather than a generic failure

title: Session refresh keeps an in-progress flow alive
preconditions: A session approaching expiry mid-transaction
steps:
1. Begin a transaction and hold past the original session lifetime
2. Let the session refresh
3. Complete the transaction
expected: The session refreshes before expiry and the transaction completes without restarting; the refresh is isolated from the registration refresh mechanism

title: A trusted device is remembered and an untrusted one is challenged
preconditions: One trusted device and one new device
steps:
1. Sign in on the trusted device
2. Sign in on the new device
expected: The trusted device follows its configured path; the new device is challenged. The device fingerprint is validated server-side, not accepted from the client

title: Lockout after repeated failures persists across surfaces
preconditions: An account able to be locked by repeated failures
steps:
1. Fail sign-in enough times to lock the account
2. Attempt to sign in on another device and through the API
expected: The lock holds on every surface and is not bypassable by switching client; unlocking follows the documented path only

title: Privileges resolved at sign-in are enforced on every surface
preconditions: A user whose role lacks a specific privilege
steps:
1. Sign in
2. Attempt the guarded action through the UI and directly against the API
expected: Both are refused; hiding the control in the UI is not the control, and the API refuses independently

title: Privilege changes take effect on the next session
preconditions: A signed-in user whose role is then changed
steps:
1. Change the user's privileges
2. Have them sign out and back in
3. Attempt the affected action
expected: The new privileges apply on the new session and are enforced at the API, not only in the UI

title: Sign-in latency holds under concurrent load
preconditions: Peak concurrent sign-in load
steps: 1. Drive sustained sign-ins and measure end-to-end latency
expected: Latency stays within the agreed budget; no session is issued to the wrong account under concurrency

title: Language choice carries from sign-in into the session
preconditions: Arabic and English both available
steps:
1. Sign in with Arabic selected
2. Move through several screens and trigger a validation error
expected: Content and error messages stay in the chosen language throughout, with no untranslated string or raw key

title: A product subscription charge reaches the wallet and the ledger consistently
preconditions: A business subscribing to a paid product
steps:
1. Complete the subscription
2. Compare wallet ledger, transaction log and the subscription record
expected: All three agree on the amount charged including commission and VAT; the wallet is debited exactly once

title: Subscribing provisions the product's capabilities end to end
preconditions: A business subscribing to a product that unlocks features
steps:
1. Complete the subscription
2. Exercise each capability the product grants
expected: Every granted capability works immediately; nothing requires a manual back-office step that is not documented

title: A product that provisions a wallet creates exactly one
preconditions: A product whose subscription provisions a wallet
steps:
1. Subscribe
2. Query the wallets created
expected: Exactly one wallet is created with the correct currency and zero opening balance across all four buckets

title: Product-level commission overrides resolve correctly
preconditions: A product with its own commission configuration
steps:
1. Complete a transaction under that product
2. Compare the fee against the expected precedence
expected: The most specific configured scheme wins and the fee entries match it exactly

title: Cancelling a product withdraws its capabilities and stops billing
preconditions: An active subscription
steps:
1. Cancel it
2. Attempt the product's capabilities
3. Wait through the next billing cycle
expected: Capabilities are withdrawn on the documented boundary and no further charge is raised

title: A PoS product subscription flows through to a device order
preconditions: A business subscribing to the PoS product
steps:
1. Complete the subscription
2. Follow through to the PoS order and TID mapping
expected: The subscription creates the expected order and the mapped TID activates on the correct main wallet

title: Product eligibility follows the registry-verified business activity
preconditions: Businesses with different Wathiq activity classifications
steps: 1. Attempt to subscribe each to a restricted product
expected: Eligibility follows the Wathiq-verified activity, not user-entered data; ineligible businesses are refused with a clear reason

title: The product catalogue loads within budget at full size
preconditions: A catalogue at production size
steps: 1. Load the catalogue and page through it, measuring response time
expected: Loads within the agreed budget and paging stays responsive

title: A customer payout reaches the bank with the verified beneficiary
preconditions: A customer with a verified beneficiary IBAN
steps:
1. Complete a payout
2. Compare the outbound instruction against the beneficiary record
expected: IBAN and name match the verified beneficiary exactly; the wallet is debited once including fees

title: A card transaction reflects in the wallet and the statement consistently
preconditions: A customer with an active card
steps:
1. Complete a card transaction
2. Compare wallet ledger, statement and card records
expected: All three agree on amount, status and timestamp

title: The customer app enforces authorisation at the API, not the UI
preconditions: A user without the privilege this feature requires
steps:
1. Confirm the control is hidden in the UI
2. Call every endpoint behind it directly, with a valid session but no privilege
expected: Every call is refused with 403; hiding a control is not a control, and a hidden button must never be the only thing standing between a user and the action

title: The customer app is scoped to the caller's own account
preconditions: Two accounts each holding records in this feature
steps: 1. As one account, request and act on the other's records by direct identifier and by guessed identifier
expected: Every attempt is refused with no leakage of the other account's data, existence or record count

title: The customer app rejects an expired, malformed or absent token
preconditions: Tokens in each state
steps: 1. Call the endpoints with no token, a malformed token and an expired token
expected: Each is refused with 401. A malformed token must not produce a 500 — rejecting bad credentials with a server error is itself a defect

title: The customer app leaks no sensitive data into logs or responses
preconditions: Traffic through this feature carrying identifiers and credentials
steps:
1. Exercise the main flows including failures
2. Search application logs, HTTP logs and error responses for PAN, OTP, password, token and national ID values
expected: None appears in plain text anywhere; error responses carry a message code rather than a stack trace or internal identifier

title: Customer identity re-verification gates sensitive actions
preconditions: A customer whose identity data needs refreshing
steps: 1. Attempt a sensitive action
expected: It is gated behind re-verification with a clear path; stale identity data does not authorise it

title: Customer notifications are delivered without leaking sensitive data
preconditions: Notifications enabled
steps:
1. Trigger transactional and OTP notifications
2. Inspect content and the notification log
expected: Each is delivered with the right content; no OTP, PAN or credential is stored in plain text

title: The customer app stays responsive on a heavy account
preconditions: An account with long history and several wallets
steps: 1. Move through balance, history and transfer flows, measuring responsiveness
expected: Each screen stays within the agreed budget and history paginates

title: The dashboard balance matches the ledger after a transaction
preconditions: A funded wallet with the dashboard open
steps:
1. Note the displayed balance
2. Complete a transaction in another session
3. Refresh the dashboard
4. Compare against the wallet ledger
expected: The displayed balance matches the ledger-derived balance exactly; the dashboard never shows a stale figure as current

title: Reserved funds are shown distinctly from spendable balance
preconditions: A wallet with an open pending outgoing transaction
steps: 1. Open the dashboard while the transaction is pending
expected: Available and reserved are presented distinctly; the customer is never shown reserved money as spendable

title: The dashboard reads the same balance the wallet service holds
preconditions: A funded wallet
steps: 1. Read the balance on the dashboard and directly from the wallet service
expected: Both agree exactly, including all four buckets; the dashboard never presents a cached figure as current

title: Displayed limits and remaining headroom match the engine
preconditions: A wallet with configured limits and some usage
steps:
1. Compare the displayed remaining headroom against what the limits engine enforces
2. Transact up to the boundary
expected: The displayed figure matches what is enforced; a customer is never shown headroom they cannot actually use

title: Switching wallets shows the right balance and history each time
preconditions: An account with several wallets holding different balances
steps: 1. Switch between wallets and compare each balance and history against its ledger
expected: Each wallet shows its own balance and history with no bleed between them

title: Switching wallet switches every dependent panel together
preconditions: An account with several wallets
steps: 1. Switch wallet and inspect balance, history, limits and quick actions
expected: Every panel switches together; no panel keeps showing the previous wallet's data

title: Every balance-changing event notifies and appears on the dashboard
preconditions: Notifications enabled on a funded wallet
steps:
1. Complete a credit and a debit
2. Inspect notifications and the dashboard
expected: Each produces a notification and a dashboard entry with matching amount and reference

title: A downloaded statement matches the on-screen history
preconditions: An account with history across a date range
steps: 1. Download the statement and compare against the on-screen history for the same range
expected: Row count, amounts and running balance agree; nothing is dropped or duplicated at the range boundaries

title: A new transaction appears in the dashboard history with correct detail
preconditions: A funded wallet
steps:
1. Complete a transaction
2. Open the dashboard history and the transaction detail
expected: The transaction appears with the correct amount, type, counterparty, fee and reference, matching the transaction log

title: The dashboard loads within budget on a heavy account
preconditions: An account with a long transaction history
steps: 1. Load the dashboard and measure time to first meaningful content
expected: It loads within the agreed budget and history paginates rather than loading in full

title: Amounts and dates render correctly in Arabic
preconditions: Arabic selected
steps: 1. Open the dashboard and its history in Arabic
expected: Amounts, currency and dates render correctly under right-to-left layout, with nothing reversed, truncated or overlapping

title: An RMS block stops the transaction before money moves
preconditions: A transaction that RMS will block
steps:
1. Attempt it
2. Inspect all four buckets on every participating wallet
expected: The transaction is stopped before any movement or reserve; nothing needs unwinding afterwards

title: An RMS rule change affects the next transaction, not past ones
preconditions: An active RMS rule
steps:
1. Change it
2. Run a transaction that the new rule affects
3. Re-inspect historical transactions
expected: The new rule applies going forward; historical transactions and their outcomes are unchanged

title: A flagged transaction reaches the review queue with its evidence
preconditions: A transaction that RMS flags for review
steps:
1. Trigger the flag
2. Open the review queue item
expected: The item carries the transaction, the rule that fired and the evidence needed to decide, and its resolution is recorded

title: Admin actions are recorded against the acting admin
preconditions: Several admins acting on the same records
steps:
1. Have each perform an audited action
2. Inspect the audit trail
expected: Each action is attributed to the admin who performed it; no action is recorded against a service account or left unattributed

title: A privilege removal reaches every surface
preconditions: A user holding a guarded privilege on web, Android and iOS
steps:
1. Remove the privilege
2. Attempt the guarded action on each client and directly against the API
expected: All four refuse; no client retains access from a cached privilege set

title: Business and admin scopes stay isolated end to end
preconditions: A business user and an admin user
steps:
1. Call the admin-scoped RBAC endpoints as the business user, and the reverse
2. Repeat through each client
expected: Neither reaches the other's scope on any surface; scope is enforced server-side

title: A privilege change invalidates what the open session may do
preconditions: A signed-in user whose privilege is revoked mid-session
steps:
1. Revoke the privilege while the session is open
2. Attempt the guarded action on that session
expected: The action is refused on the existing session per the documented refresh rule; a live session must not outlive its privileges indefinitely

title: A privilege gate blocks the money action, not just its button
preconditions: A user without the transfer privilege
steps: 1. Attempt a transfer through the UI and directly against the API
expected: Both are refused and no transaction or reserve is created; hiding the control is not the control

title: Every privilege change is audit-logged and traceable
preconditions: Audit log accessible
steps:
1. Grant and then remove a privilege
2. Inspect the audit trail
expected: Both changes are recorded with actor, target, previous and new values, and timestamp

title: Effective privileges resolve correctly for a user in several groups
preconditions: A user belonging to two groups with overlapping and conflicting roles
steps:
1. Determine the expected effective set
2. Exercise guarded actions across both
expected: Effective privileges resolve as documented; no privilege is silently gained from group overlap

title: A privilege grant is usable without re-provisioning
preconditions: A user gaining a new privilege
steps:
1. Grant it
2. Have the user reach the newly permitted action
expected: The action becomes available on the documented refresh path, with no manual account rebuild

title: Privilege resolution does not degrade with group count
preconditions: A user in many groups with many privileges
steps: 1. Measure sign-in and first-action latency as group count grows
expected: Latency stays flat; resolution does not scale with configuration volume

title: A sub-wallet movement reflects in the parent position
preconditions: A parent wallet with several sub-wallets
steps:
1. Move funds into and out of a sub-wallet
2. Compare the parent's position and the sub-wallet ledgers
expected: The parent position equals the sum of its sub-wallets plus its own balance at every point; nothing is double-counted between the two levels

title: Sub-wallet rules are enforced by the rules engine, not the UI
preconditions: A sub-wallet linked to a spending rule
steps: 1. Attempt a movement that breaches the rule through the UI and directly against the API
expected: Both are refused server-side by the rules engine with the same reason

title: Sub-wallet activity counts against the parent's limits
preconditions: A parent near its limit with an active sub-wallet
steps: 1. Attempt a sub-wallet transaction that would breach the parent limit
expected: It is refused; limits are evaluated against the combined position, not the sub-wallet alone

title: Sub-wallet management responds within budget at production volume
preconditions: Production-scale data and a representative load profile
steps:
1. Exercise the main sub-wallet management flows under load
2. Measure response time at p50, p95 and p99
3. Capture the query plans behind each list and search
expected: Each flow stays within its agreed budget at p99; queries use indexed access with no full-table scan, and paging stays responsive at depth

title: Sub-wallet management holds up under concurrent use
preconditions: Several users acting on the same records concurrently
steps:
1. Drive concurrent reads and writes against the same records
2. Reconcile the final state against what was submitted
expected: No record is lost, duplicated or left partially written; concurrent writers either serialise or fail cleanly, and nothing is silently overwritten

title: Sub-wallet management degrades gracefully when a dependency is slow
preconditions: A downstream dependency responding slowly or failing
steps:
1. Introduce latency, then failure, at the dependency
2. Observe the feature and everything around it
expected: The affected operation times out cleanly with a retry path and a readable message; unrelated operations and other users are unaffected, and nothing is left half-applied

title: Removing a user revokes their access immediately
preconditions: An active staff user with an open session
steps:
1. Remove the user
2. Use their still-open session
expected: The session is invalidated and every authenticated call is refused

title: An approved beneficiary becomes usable across every payment flow
preconditions: A beneficiary moving from PENDING to APPROVED
steps:
1. Approve the beneficiary
2. Use it in a bill, a transfer and a payout
expected: It is selectable and usable in all three; a PENDING or REJECTED beneficiary is refused in all three with the same reason

title: A user added through Manage Users receives exactly the intended privileges
preconditions: A newly added staff user with a chosen role
steps:
1. Add the user and assign the role
2. Sign in as them and probe both permitted and forbidden actions
expected: They hold exactly the role's privileges — no more, no less — enforced at the API

title: Beneficiary OTP issue and resend both work end to end
preconditions: A beneficiary being added
steps:
1. Trigger the beneficiary OTP
2. Resend it
3. Complete verification
expected: Both issue successfully — not 500 and not 403 — and the beneficiary is added on verification (EMI-5692, EMI-5769, EMI-5800)

title: Profile identity changes re-verify through the identity provider
preconditions: A profile change touching a verified identity field
steps: 1. Attempt the change
expected: The change requires re-verification rather than accepting user input over provider data

title: Profile and account management responds within budget at production volume
preconditions: Production-scale data and a representative load profile
steps:
1. Exercise the main profile and account management flows under load
2. Measure response time at p50, p95 and p99
3. Capture the query plans behind each list and search
expected: Each flow stays within its agreed budget at p99; queries use indexed access with no full-table scan, and paging stays responsive at depth

title: Profile and account management holds up under concurrent use
preconditions: Several users acting on the same records concurrently
steps:
1. Drive concurrent reads and writes against the same records
2. Reconcile the final state against what was submitted
expected: No record is lost, duplicated or left partially written; concurrent writers either serialise or fail cleanly, and nothing is silently overwritten

title: Profile and user-management changes notify the right people
preconditions: Notifications enabled
steps:
1. Add a user, change a role and update profile details
2. Inspect notifications and the log
expected: Each change notifies the correct recipients with accurate content and no sensitive value in plain text

title: Profile and account management degrades gracefully when a dependency is slow
preconditions: A downstream dependency responding slowly or failing
steps:
1. Introduce latency, then failure, at the dependency
2. Observe the feature and everything around it
expected: The affected operation times out cleanly with a retry path and a readable message; unrelated operations and other users are unaffected, and nothing is left half-applied

title: Full password recovery, then sign in with the new password
preconditions: An active account with a reachable OTP channel
steps:
1. Request a reset
2. Verify the OTP
3. Set a new password
4. Sign in with it, then attempt the old one
expected: Recovery completes; the new password works and the old one is refused everywhere

title: Existing sessions are invalidated by a password change
preconditions: An account signed in on a second device
steps:
1. Complete a password reset on device one
2. Use the still-open session on device two
expected: The other session is invalidated and its token refused; a password change must not leave a live session behind

title: A recovery OTP cannot be reused or used past expiry
preconditions: A reset in progress

steps: 1. Attempt every money-moving action directly against the API
expected: All are refused server-side; hiding controls in the app is not the control

title: WS1 screens both the company and its authorised person
preconditions: A business application reaching the screening step
steps:
1. Submit the application
2. Capture the WS1 request and inspect what was screened
expected: WS1 is called with both the company and the authorised person; screening only one of the two is a regulatory gap, not a shortcut

title: A WS1 sanctions or PEP hit stops the application
preconditions: An applicant that WS1 will return a hit for
steps:
1. Submit the application
2. Observe the outcome and any created account or wallet
expected: The application is stopped and routed for review; no account or wallet is provisioned while a hit is open

title: A WS1 hit is never disclosed to the applicant
preconditions: An applicant with a WS1 hit
steps: 1. Read every applicant-facing message and status
expected: The applicant sees a neutral pending or declined state; no wording reveals a screening hit, its source or its category. Tipping off is a regulatory breach, not a UX detail

title: WS1 unavailable fails closed, never open
preconditions: WS1 made unreachable
steps:
1. Submit an application
2. Observe whether it can proceed
expected: The application waits and is retried; it must never proceed as screened when screening did not run. Failing open here provisions an unscreened account

title: WS3 runs as the final consolidated check before the account is usable
preconditions: An application that has passed WS1
steps:
1. Follow the application to completion
2. Capture the WS3 call and its position in the sequence
expected: WS3 runs after WS1 and before the account becomes transactable; its result gates activation

title: WS3 cannot be reached without a completed WS1
preconditions: An application whose WS1 has not completed
steps: 1. Attempt to drive the application to the WS3 stage
expected: WS3 is not called and the application cannot skip ahead; the order of the two gates is enforced server-side

title: A WS3 hit blocks activation even though WS1 passed
preconditions: An application that clears WS1 but is flagged at WS3
steps:
1. Complete the application
2. Attempt to transact
expected: Activation is blocked and the case is routed for review; a clean WS1 does not override a WS3 hit

title: The WS3 result is recorded with enough detail for a regulator
preconditions: A completed WS3 screening
steps: 1. Inspect the stored screening record
expected: The record carries the request, the provider response, the decision, the timestamp and the actor, and is immutable and retained per policy

title: MOZN non-financial events are delivered and recorded
preconditions: MOZN event delivery configured
steps:
1. Trigger the non-financial events MOZN expects
2. Inspect delivery and the stored record
expected: Each event is delivered with the agreed payload and recorded; a delivery failure is retried and alarmed rather than dropped (EMI-6042)

title: Screening runs once per application, not once per retry
preconditions: An application resubmitted after a validation error
steps:
1. Trigger several resubmissions
2. Count the screening calls and cases raised
expected: Screening is not re-run for an unchanged applicant on every resubmission; duplicate cases are not created at the provider

title: A WS1 timeout is retried without duplicating the screening
preconditions: WS1 responding slowly, then recovering
steps:
1. Let the call time out
2. Let the retry succeed
3. Inspect the screening records
expected: One screening result is recorded for the application; a retry does not create a second case or a second charge

title: Screening latency does not stall onboarding at peak
preconditions: Concurrent applications at campaign volume
steps:
1. Drive concurrent applications through WS1 and WS3
2. Measure step latency and queue depth
expected: Screening completes within the agreed budget and a backlog degrades gracefully rather than failing applications

title: Screening records are immutable and retained
preconditions: Historical screening records
steps:
1. Attempt to update or delete one
2. Query records at the far end of the retention window
expected: Updates and deletes are refused; records remain queryable for the full retention period

title: KYC, KYB and AML screening responds within budget at production volume
preconditions: Production-scale data and a representative load profile
steps:
1. Exercise the main kyc, kyb and aml screening flows under load
2. Measure response time at p50, p95 and p99
3. Capture the query plans behind each list and search
expected: Each flow stays within its agreed budget at p99; queries use indexed access with no full-table scan, and paging stays responsive at depth

title: KYC, KYB and AML screening holds up under concurrent use
preconditions: Several users acting on the same records concurrently
steps:
1. Drive concurrent reads and writes against the same records
2. Reconcile the final state against what was submitted
expected: No record is lost, duplicated or left partially written; concurrent writers either serialise or fail cleanly, and nothing is silently overwritten

title: KYC, KYB and AML screening degrades gracefully when a dependency is slow
preconditions: A downstream dependency responding slowly or failing
steps:
1. Introduce latency, then failure, at the dependency
2. Observe the feature and everything around it
expected: The affected operation times out cleanly with a retry path and a readable message; unrelated operations and other users are unaffected, and nothing is left half-applied

title: A configuration change does not retrospectively alter existing wallets
preconditions: Wallets created under the previous configuration
steps:
1. Change the configuration
2. Inspect existing wallets and their balances
expected: Existing wallets and their balances are unchanged; the new rule applies going forward only

title: A configuration change reaches the wallet service
preconditions: An active wallet configuration
steps:
1. Change a rule
2. Exercise the affected behaviour without restarting anything
expected: The new rule applies immediately and the previous value stops applying

title: Wallet-level limits are enforced alongside transaction limits
preconditions: A wallet with both a balance ceiling and transaction limits
steps: 1. Attempt movements that breach each in turn
expected: Each is refused with the correct, distinguishable reason; the two limit types are evaluated independently

title: Wallet configuration responds within budget at production volume

steps:

title: Taqnyat delivers the OTP across every flow that needs one
preconditions: Taqnyat configured; accounts able to reach each OTP flow
steps:
1. Trigger the OTP in login, registration, transaction, beneficiary add and password reset
2. Confirm delivery for each
expected: An OTP is delivered in every flow through the configured channel, and the notification log records each send

title: No OTP is ever stored in plain text
preconditions: OTP traffic across every flow
steps:
1. Trigger OTPs across all flows
2. Search the Notification Log and the Taqnyat HTTP Log in MongoDB for the values
expected: Every stored copy is hashed; no plain-text OTP is persisted in either collection (EMI-5913, EMI-5808)

title: An OTP cannot be reused once consumed
preconditions: A completed OTP verification
steps: 1. Replay the same OTP on the same flow
expected: The replay is refused; a consumed OTP is dead regardless of its remaining validity window

title: An expired OTP is refused and a fresh one can be requested
preconditions: An OTP left past its validity window
steps:
1. Submit the expired code
2. Request a new one and complete verification
expected: The expired code is refused with a clear reason and the new one succeeds

title: Repeated wrong OTPs lock the attempt per the documented rule
preconditions: An OTP flow in progress
steps:
1. Submit wrong codes past the configured attempt limit
2. Observe the lock and its recovery path
expected: The attempt locks per the rule and recovers only on the documented path; the account is not left permanently unreachable and the lock is not bypassable by restarting the flow

title: An OTP issued for one flow does not work in another
preconditions: OTPs issued in two different flows for the same customer
steps: 1. Take the OTP issued for a transaction and submit it in the password-reset flow, and the reverse
expected: Each is refused; OTPs are scoped to the flow and operation that issued them

title: An OTP issued for one customer never verifies for another
preconditions: OTPs issued for two customers
steps: 1. Submit customer A's code against customer B's session
expected: Refused; codes are bound to the issuing identity

title: A delivery failure is retried and alarmed, never dropped silently
preconditions: The notification provider made unreachable
steps:
1. Trigger notifications during the outage
2. Restore the provider
expected: Failed deliveries are retried per policy and alarmed after the configured attempts; none is silently discarded

title: Only Taqnyat carries OTP data in the HTTP log
preconditions: Traffic across Wathiq, Nafath, Yaqeen, Taqnyat, Lean, MOZN, HyperPay, WS1, WS3 and ANB
steps:
1. Exercise each integration
2. Search the HTTP log per integration for OTP-related content
expected: Only Taqnyat carries OTP data, and it is hashed. Any other integration storing it is a finding

title: Resend issues a working code without invalidating the flow
preconditions: An OTP flow in progress
steps:
1. Request a resend
2. Verify with the newest code
3. Then try the superseded one
expected: Resend succeeds — not 500 and not 403 — the newest code works, and the superseded code is refused (EMI-5692, EMI-5769, EMI-5800)

title: Resend is rate limited without locking the customer out permanently
preconditions: An OTP flow in progress
steps:
1. Request resend repeatedly past the configured limit
2. Wait out the window and retry
expected: Further resends are refused while the limit holds, the customer is told when they can retry, and the flow recovers afterwards

title: Provider failure is surfaced without consuming the attempt
preconditions: Taqnyat made unreachable
steps:
1. Trigger an OTP send
2. Restore the provider and retry
expected: The customer is told delivery failed and can retry; the failed send does not count against the resend or attempt limits, and the failure is logged and alarmed

title: OTP settings changed by an admin take effect without a release
preconditions: Admin access to OTP configuration
steps:
1. Change the validity window, length and attempt limit
2. Run an OTP flow against the new values
expected: The new configuration applies immediately; the change is audit-logged with actor and previous value

title: Notification language follows the recipient's locale
preconditions: Recipients configured for Arabic and English
steps: 1. Trigger the same notification for each
expected: Each arrives in the recipient's language with correct interpolation and no untranslated string or raw key

title: Disabling OTP for a flow is honoured consistently
preconditions: A flow whose OTP requirement can be toggled
steps:
1. Disable it and run the flow
2. Re-enable and run again
expected: The flow skips or requires OTP exactly as configured, on every client and at the API

title: Notification throughput holds during a burst
preconditions: A burst of balance-changing events
steps: 1. Drive the burst and measure delivery latency and loss
expected: Delivery stays within the agreed budget and nothing is lost; the queue drains rather than dropping messages

title: Wallet-to-wallet transfer moves money and reconciles on both sides
preconditions: Two active wallets, sender funded
steps:
1. Complete a W2W transfer
2. Read both wallets' four buckets and both ledgers
3. Compare against the transaction log
expected: Sender debited and receiver credited by the same amount net of fees; both ledgers and the transaction log agree; current = available + reserve_debit holds on both wallets

title: Cross-wallet conservation holds during the reserve window
preconditions: A transfer with commission and VAT legs
steps:
1. Initiate the transfer and hold it in the reserve window
2. Sum reserve_credit across receiver, commission and VAT wallets
3. Compare with the sender's reserve_debit
expected: The sender's reserve_debit equals the sum of reserve_credit across all destination wallets. A shortfall means a leg was never created and is a defect, not a rounding difference

title: A failed transfer returns both parties to their starting position
preconditions: A transfer that will fail after reserving
steps:
1. Record both wallets' four buckets
2. Initiate the transfer and force the failure
3. Re-read all buckets
expected: Both wallets return exactly to their starting position, including the commission and VAT wallets; no reserve is stranded on any leg

title: A duplicate submission produces one transfer
preconditions: A transfer able to be submitted twice
steps:
1. Submit the same transfer twice
2. Inspect transactions and both balances
expected: Exactly one transfer exists; the sender is debited once and the receiver credited once

title: Wallet-to-wallet transfer enforces authorisation at the API, not the UI
preconditions: A user without the privilege this feature requires
steps:
1. Confirm the control is hidden in the UI
2. Call every endpoint behind it directly, with a valid session but no privilege
expected: Every call is refused with 403; hiding a control is not a control, and a hidden button must never be the only thing standing between a user and the action

title: Wallet-to-wallet transfer is scoped to the caller's own account
preconditions: Two accounts each holding records in this feature
steps: 1. As one account, request and act on the other's records by direct identifier and by guessed identifier
expected: Every attempt is refused with no leakage of the other account's data, existence or record count

title: Wallet-to-wallet transfer rejects an expired, malformed or absent token
preconditions: Tokens in each state
steps: 1. Call the endpoints with no token, a malformed token and an expired token
expected: Each is refused with 401. A malformed token must not produce a 500 — rejecting bad credentials with a server error is itself a defect

title: Wallet-to-wallet transfer leaks no sensitive data into logs or responses
preconditions: Traffic through this feature carrying identifiers and credentials
steps:
1. Exercise the main flows including failures
2. Search application logs, HTTP logs and error responses for PAN, OTP, password, token and national ID values
expected: None appears in plain text anywhere; error responses carry a message code rather than a stack trace or internal identifier

title: Commission and VAT post to their own wallets and reconcile
preconditions: A transfer type with commission configured
steps:
1. Complete a transfer
2. Read the commission and VAT wallet ledgers
expected: Commission and VAT land in their own wallets exactly once, and the sum of every leg equals the amount taken from the sender to the halalah

title: Sender and receiver limits are both enforced
preconditions: A sender near their limit and a receiver near their balance ceiling
steps:
1. Attempt a transfer breaching the sender's limit
2. Attempt one breaching the receiver's ceiling
expected: Each is refused with the correct reason and nothing moves in either case

expected: The export contains only the scoped rows and columns; no hidden sheet, column or metadata field carries other customers data or internal identifiers

expected: Both are recorded with actor, report type, scope, parameters and timestamp, so an extract of customer financial data is always attributable

steps: 1. Generate the report
expected: An empty report is produced with zero totals and a clear empty state; it does not error or return a blank file

2. Reconcile the totals against the ledger
expected: It completes within its budget and every total still ties to the ledger; a span one day beyond the maximum is refused with a clear message rather than timing out
